formosa-ha-tinh-marine-disaster.whole: Formosa Ha Tinh's total investment in the steel complex was nearly US$13 billion (The Investor, 2022). The company said it produced 6.5 million tonnes of steel in 2021, about 500,000 tonnes more than in 2020. It has run at a loss in recent years: about VND8 trillion (about US$333 million) in 2022, and VND15.7 trillion (about US$654 million) in 2023, according to Vietnam Investment Review, which took the 2023 figure from the parent Formosa Plastics Group's annual financial statement (the same article's headline gives VND16 trillion, about US$666.7 million). These are the company's own figures; no independent check was found.

ok-tedi-fly-river.whole: Ok Tedi was PNG's biggest mine in 2018, with revenue of K529 million, according to the 2018 PNG Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative report (Business Advantage PNG). Ok Tedi Mining says it produced 106,018 tonnes of copper and 298,350 ounces of gold in 2025, on unaudited revenue of K9.3 billion (US$2.3 billion). It lists K1.09 billion in taxes, K178 million in royalties, K1 billion in dividends and K99 million in compensation as benefits from that year's results. The 2025 figures are the company's own; no independent check was found.

bodo-shell-oil-spills.whole: The Trans Niger Pipeline, the line that leaked near Bodo in 2008 (IBTimes UK), can carry about 180,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day and feeds the Bonny export terminal (Ecofin Agency, 2017). In April 2025, NOSDRA, Nigeria's oil spill regulator, said 355 of the 363 cleanup grids at Bodo had been cleared and certified, and that full restoration could begin (ThisDay). Shell sold its Nigerian onshore subsidiary SPDC to the Renaissance consortium; the sale closed on 13 March 2025 (S&P Global). NOSDRA's director general told Renaissance that the remaining work was 'no longer a Shell responsibility' but theirs (ThisDay).

cape-asbestos-northern-cape.whole: Cape Asbestos was registered in Britain and began in 1893. It mined at Koegas and Prieska and shipped almost all of its output to its own factories in Britain, Italy and France and to other buyers. It came close to a monopoly in 1937, when it took over all of Dominion Blue's assets, and it had more than 1,000 labourers in 1938. Snyman wrote that the Northern Cape belt produced almost all of the world's blue asbestos. Its blue asbestos arm, Cape Blue Mines, left the industry in 1981. All of these points come from P.H.R. Snyman's 1988 history in the journal Historia.

areva-arlit-akokan-radiation.whole: Somair at Arlit produced 3,065 tonnes of uranium at its 2012 peak, falling to 959 tonnes in 2024. Cominak at Akokan produced about 75,000 tonnes before it closed in March 2021. These figures come from the World Nuclear Association, a trade body for the nuclear industry that lists the operator Orano among its sources; no independent check was found. The association also reports that Niger stopped exports of Somair uranium after the July 2023 coup, that Orano said in December 2024 it had lost operational control of the mine, that Niger nationalised Somair in June 2025, and that in May 2026 the government adopted draft decrees to cancel the Arlit concession and hand it to a new state company, TSUMCO.

thar-jath-oil-water-pollution.whole: Eye Radio reported that Thar Jath began producing in 2006 at about 40,000 barrels a day, peaked at 54,000 in 2009 and fell to 4,500 in 2014 before stopping in the civil war. It reported that national output fell from 265,000 to 165,000 barrels a day during the shutdown and that oil pays for 98% of the national budget. Production restarted on 21 June 2021, after a shutdown Eye Radio's headline puts at 7 years and its text at 'nearly 8 years'. SPOC's head, Eruwan Gerry, said the operator aimed for 8,000 barrels a day by the end of 2021 and 16,000 by mid-2022; these were targets, not results. In November 2025 Petroleum Ministry undersecretary Deng Lual Wol said operations at Tharjiath were back to normal after drone attacks on the Heglig facility in Sudan disrupted exports (AP via WTOP). No independent check of these figures was found.

mandalika-lombok-evictions.whole: By the AIIB's own monitoring report covering January-October 2024, US$122.6 million of the US$248.4 million loan (49%) had been paid out by 25 September 2024. By then 18.5 of 25.95 km of roads and 3.6 of 24.6 km of piped water had been built. No wastewater network, treatment plant, power network or solid waste facility had been built yet; their tenders were still pending. Reported results were 40,869 overnight tourists against a target of 200,000, and 440 local residents employed in tourism against 2,539. The closing date was moved from September 2024 to September 2026. These are the lender's own figures; no independent check was found.

kodaikanal-unilever-mercury.whole: Chesebrough Pond's moved its mercury thermometer factory from the US to Kodaikanal in 1983, and Hindustan Lever took it over in 1986. Until 2001 the factory produced 163 million thermometers, using about 900 kg of mercury a year, for export to the US and Europe; the article does not say whether 163 million was a yearly or total figure. It ran two shifts of 200 workers in 1984-1989, and more than 1,000 people worked there over its life. It was ordered shut in early 2001. All of these figures come from Business Standard (2016).

bhabadah-waterlogging-kjdrp.whole: The project planned 355 km of canals, 29 km of rebuilt embankments, 30 km of roads and 21 bridges; in 1999 Down To Earth reported only 20% of the work done. ADB's own evaluation in 2007 rated the project 'unsuccessful, bordering on partly successful', and also rated it inefficient and 'unlikely sustainable'. The evaluation found cropping intensity rose in both the project area and a comparison area outside it, so it did not credit the project with the rise. It also found silt blocking canals and regulators, poor upkeep, and membership in water management groups falling from 37% at completion to 15% in 2007. Apart from the 1999 press report, the figures come from the lender's own evaluation; no independent outcome figures were found.

vale-moatize-cateme.whole: The Moatize mine began producing in August 2011. It exports coal by the 912 km Nacala rail corridor, which runs through Malawi to the port of Nacala-a-Velha (NS Energy). NS Energy reported output of 6.1 million tonnes of metallurgical coal and 5.4 million tonnes of thermal coal in 2018, 4.03 and 4.73 million tonnes in 2019 (about 8.8 million tonnes in all), and 5.87 million tonnes in 2020, against a planned capacity of 18 million tonnes a year. In December 2021 Vale agreed to sell the mine and the corridor to Jindal's Vulcan Minerals for up to US$270 million (NS Energy). NS Energy does not say where its production figures come from; no independent check was found.

The port, which can dock large ships and passenger ferries, cost about €100 million. The runway was extended to about 600 metres. The article also reported government spending of about €200 million on housing blocks and other planned projects, including water systems, a junior high school and a police station. firestone-liberia-taylor-deal.whole: Under its 1926 concession, Firestone could lease up to 1 million acres, about 10% of Liberia's arable land, at six cents an acre for 99 years. It became Liberia's largest private employer and largest exporter, and one study found its 1951 after-tax profits were three times the Liberian government's total revenue that year (ProPublica/Frontline). Today it runs a plantation of almost 480 km² with more than 4,000 employees and buys rubber from independent farmers (AFP via Taipei Times, July 2026). The same report said Liberia's rubber output was 73,769 tonnes in 2025, by the Central Bank of Liberia's count, and that rubber made up about 2.2% of GDP.

ioi-ketapang-peatland-clearing.whole: IOI reported 21,332 hectares of oil palm planted in Indonesia in its 2023 integrated report (financial year to 30 June 2023). That is part of a group total of 176,925 hectares, whose mills produced 580,688 tonnes of crude palm oil that year. In December 2016 IOI agreed with the complainant Aidenvironment to abandon a further 434 hectares cleared and planted in 2010-2014 at PT BNS, remove overplanted palms in Ketapang, and not sell oil from PT BNS and the affected areas of PT SKS as RSPO-certified for one planting cycle (The Star). central-kalahari-san-evictions-gope.whole: Gem Diamonds bought the Gope deposit from De Beers in 2007 and spent about US$85 million building the Ghaghoo underground mine, which came online in 2015 (Mining Index; MiningMX). It recovered fewer than 150,000 carats before going onto care and maintenance in early 2017, and an earthquake in 2017 flooded it (Mining Index). Gem announced a US$5.4 million sale to Pro Civil in 2019 (MiningMX) and a US$4 million sale to Okwa Diamonds in 2021 (Mining Index). In April 2024 Mmegi reported that Gem had spent US$1.9 million on care and maintenance in 2022 and was considering cutting its skeleton staff. The figures come from the company as reported in the press; no independent check was found.

kamoa-kakula-muvunda-resettlement.whole: Ivanhoe Mines reported that Kamoa-Kakula produced 437,061 tonnes of copper in 2024, up 12% on 2023 (Bankable, January 2025). Bankable found a US$470 million gap between the sales figure it calculated and the one the company reported, and said the company had not explained it despite inquiries. kilembe-tailings-nyamwamba.whole: Kilembe began producing in 1956 and exporting in 1959, and it peaked at about 18,000 tonnes of copper cathode a year. In 1965 minerals made up 14% of Uganda's export earnings, with copper third behind coffee and cotton (Daily Monitor, 2017). Mining stopped in 1978. In March 2025 Uganda signed a production sharing agreement with two local firms, Sarrai Group and Nile Fibreboard, to restart it; no investment amount or output target was given (Creamer Media). As of 8 February 2026, eight months after the handover, Nile Post reported little visible work at the mine, and a local leader said he had expected at least preparatory work by then.

marange-diamond-joint-ventures.whole: The Kimberley Process recorded 7.15 million carats of diamonds exported from Zimbabwe in 2011 (NewsDay, August 2012). By August 2012, NewsDay reported, US$41.6 million of diamond money had reached the treasury, against US$600 million projected for the year. In November 2012 the campaign group Partnership Africa Canada estimated that at least US$2 billion in Marange diamonds had been stolen, calling it a conservative figure, and Finance Minister Tendai Biti said only a quarter of the US$600 million promised for his 2012 budget had arrived; government officials called the report 'totally false' (AP via Washington Times). In 2015 President Mugabe said US$15 billion of diamonds had been taken out of Marange. Journalist Nelson Banya, writing for ZimFact, said there was no evidence for Mugabe's figure, which would have needed about 40 million carats a year (Engineering News, 2018).

nouadhibou-fishmeal-factories.whole: By Mongabay's figures, Mauritania's fishmeal output rose from 111,866 tonnes in 2017 to a peak of 128,789 tonnes in 2020, then fell to 59,158 tonnes in 2024 (Mongabay, January 2026). Factories employed 1,972 people in 2019 (FAO, cited by Mongabay), and China took 68% of fishmeal and fish oil exports in 2023 (fisheries ministry data). After tighter rules from 2021, the ministry withdrew six of Nouadhibou's 30 plant licences and Mongabay found seven plants abandoned; eight of the remaining 17 were operating in September 2025. A fisheries ministry official said the policy is to phase out fishmeal gradually, keeping only the processing of fish offal.

pinpet-iron-mine-pa-o-land.whole: Construction began in 2004, and the project had an agreement worth €137 million with Russia's Tyazhpromexport. It was expected to produce 200,000 tonnes of pig iron and 720,000 tonnes of iron ore a year (The Irrawaddy, 2021). It was scheduled to start in late 2016 but was halted in March 2017, when 24 loss-making state factories were inspected; no production figures were reported. After the 2021 coup the military government moved to restart it with Russian help. On 8 March 2026 an oxygen and nitrogen plant serving the mill began commercial operation (state media MRTV, via SHAN); as of then the regime expected up to 200,000 tonnes of pig iron a year, but SHAN did not report that pig iron was being produced.

tigyit-coal-mine-power-plant.whole: Global Energy Monitor lists the plant at 120 MW in two 60 MW units, started in 2004 and 2005; a January 2011 Pa-Oh Youth Organisation report put its output at about 600 GWh a year from about 640,000 tonnes of coal, a dated estimate rather than a measured recent figure. The plant was shut in 2014 over waste management, relicensed in 2015 and restarted in 2017, and the government extended its operation to 2022. In April 2022 the Eden Group president and his son were arrested over alleged losses of 25.3 billion kyat (about US$13.6 million) while running the plant from 2018 to 2021 (Global Energy Monitor).

bohai-penglai-oil-spill.whole: Penglai 19-3 was described as China's biggest offshore oilfield; its main floating production vessel, which started production in May 2009, was designed to handle 190,000 barrels of oil a day (Offshore Technology; a design capacity, not actual output). After the 2011 leaks the operator, ConocoPhillips China, was ordered in early September to halt all operations, and CNOOC estimated output fell by 62,000 barrels a day as a result; in April 2012 China's State Oceanic Administration announced 1.683 billion yuan in compensation: 1.09 billion yuan plus 113 million yuan from ConocoPhillips China and 480 million yuan from CNOOC (Reuters, published by Fox Business on 27 April 2012). CNOOC took over as operator from ConocoPhillips in July 2014 (Offshore Technology).

kachin-rare-earth-mines.whole: Global Witness found that Myanmar exported about 19,500 tonnes of heavy rare earth oxides to China in 2021 and 41,700 tonnes in 2023, more than double China's own domestic mining quota, with the 2023 trade worth US$1.4 billion. It calls Myanmar the single largest source of heavy rare earths, but found no figures for how much of the money reaches militias or the military; the Kachin Independence Organisation says mining income goes to a regional development fund, which Global Witness could not verify.

cairo-zabbaleen-waste-contracts.whole: Under the 2003 contracts the foreign firms collected from street bins at central points and were expected to recycle only 20% of what they collected; residents complained there were too few bins, often badly placed (Al-Ahram, October 2012). No collection-rate figure for the firms was found. In September 2026 Reuters reported that Cairo still has no unified waste system, that academic research has estimated the Zabbaleen may collect about half of Cairo's waste and recycle some 80% of that, and that a World Bank-funded plant near Cairo aims to process up to 15,000 tons a day (a plan).

gautam-buddha-airport-adb-land.whole: The airport opened as Nepal's second international airport on 16 May 2022, with a 3,000-metre runway; it cost Rs40 billion including Rs28 billion for land, and ADB provided US$37 million and the OPEC Fund about US$11 million in loans (Kathmandu Post). By the airport's own count, it handled 729 international flights and 45,573 international passengers in the 31.5 months to January 2025, a period that included a roughly 10-month suspension of flights (The Rising Nepal, via Spotlight). In February 2026 the Kathmandu Post reported international services were still irregular for lack of passengers, with Thai AirAsia's twice-weekly flights struggling to fill seats.

nagarhole-ecodevelopment-relocation.whole: The GEF evaluation office's 2005 review rated the India Ecodevelopment Project's outcomes moderately satisfactory (the World Bank's own completion report said satisfactory). Across the seven sites about 580 village ecodevelopment committees were set up, against an original target of 806, and protection was strengthened over 6,020 square kilometres; the review found management costs about 60% above plan, limited biodiversity data, and some ecologically important villages left out. The project closed in June 2004, two years late; the review gives no Nagarhole-specific figures.

iwip-weda-bay-halmahera.whole: In October 2026 CELIOS researchers, citing CNBC Indonesia, reported that the park employs about 117,000 workers and that President Prabowo had launched 11 industrial projects there worth US$10.2 billion; four factories had begun commercial operation and seven had only broken ground. Investment minister Rosan has said nickel processing makes up about half of North Maluku's economy; that is a government claim, and no independent production or growth figures were found.

tsumeb-smelter-arsenic.whole: The Namibian Sun reported in August 2024 that Dundee began investing about US$515 million in the smelter soon after buying it in 2010, including a sulphuric acid plant that, by Dundee's account, turns 98% of sulphur dioxide into acid, sold mainly to the Rössing uranium mine; the smelter employed more than 1,300 people (its legal representative) and smelted 52,900 tonnes of concentrate in April-June 2024, against a record 232,000 tonnes in 2018 (no source named). Mining.com reported, without naming a source, that sulphur dioxide emissions fell 95% from 2014 to 2021 and that average arsenic exposure fell 72% since 2012 under an arsenic advisory council. In March 2024 Dundee agreed to sell the smelter to a subsidiary of China's Sinomine for US$49 million. No independent check of these figures was found.

herakles-sgsoc-cameroon.whole: A November 2013 presidential decree cut the concession from about 73,000 to 19,843 hectares and gave the company three years to develop it; in six years it cleared only about 600 hectares, according to Samuel Nguiffo of the Center for the Environment and Development (Mongabay, 2016). Herakles Farms abandoned its operations there on 29 May 2015 (SEFE, via Business and Human Rights Resource Centre), and Greenpeace reported in May 2016 that it appeared to have sold the project to new investors, with more than 500 hectares bulldozed in the following eight months. No palm oil production from SGSOC was found as of this search (November 2026).

In May 2026 The Nation reported that construction never really got going and that Thailand and Japan had withdrawn; in 2025 Russia signed an agreement, approved by the military government, to develop a port, power plant and industrial estate there (a plan).

ternium-las-encinas-aquila.whole: In its 2024 filing to the US Securities and Exchange Commission, Ternium reported paying Mexican federal authorities about US$8.1 million for Las Encinas in 2024: US$4.3 million in taxes to the tax authority and about US$3.8 million to the Ministry of Economy, with no royalties to government listed; the filing does not cover payments to the Aquila community. boliden-promel-arica-waste.whole: Chile's 2012 polymetals law (Ley 20.590) set up a state programme for affected Arica residents: care at an environmental health centre and a polymetals education grant (ChileAtiende). It also ordered more than 800 uninhabitable houses in Cerro Chuño demolished, but about 15% of residents had been relocated when demolitions stopped in 2013, a housing agency report to the court counted 793 houses still standing, and courts halted demolitions in 2017; in June 2024 El Mostrador reported no sign of a plan to clear the area.

los-pinares-guapinol-nucor.whole: In January 2023 company executives told Bloomberg Línea the project was a US$180 million investment with more than 3,000 direct jobs planned, 800 of them already held by local residents; the article also described plans for 800,000 tonnes of iron-oxide pellets and US$190 million in exports in the first year. These are company plans; no production or export results were found, and no independent check was found. In June 2023 environment minister Lucky Medina announced the mine's suspension until 2025 because licences for lot ASP II had not been approved, and La Prensa reported more than 800 jobs would be lost. In January 2025 Tocoa's mayor granted the company new operating permits (CESPAD).

harvard-caracol-campo-largo-bahia.whole: A 2014 Bahia state report found less than 300 of Campo Largo's roughly 140,000 hectares used for corn, beans, soy and eucalyptus and about 14,000 hectares used as pasture for 3,200 cattle, and a Rede Social visit in March 2017 found staff down from 84 to 50 (Mongabay, 2018). In 2018 GRAIN and Rede Social estimated Harvard had spent over US$1 billion on farmland worldwide in the previous decade, nearly 300,000 hectares of it in Brazil's Cerrado, and reported that the endowment wrote down its natural-resources portfolio by US$1.1 billion. Harvard Management Company does not comment on specific investments.

cesar-coal-hatillo-plan-bonito-resettlem.whole: Colombia's environmental licensing agency ANLA reported, with figures as of September 2020, that of 202 El Hatillo families due to be resettled, 13 had moved individually and the land chosen for collective resettlement had not been bought; Boquerón's resettlement (562 households) was still at an early stage; Plan Bonito families moved from 2014. Nearly six years later, in May 2026, Drummond said 200 El Hatillo families had been resettled and handed the vacated properties to the municipality (company's own account; no independent check found). In February 2021 Glencore announced its Prodeco unit, which produced 3.8 million tonnes of coal in 2020, would hand its Cesar mining contracts back to the state (Reuters via Mining.com).

ilisu-dam-hasankeyf.whole: The dam began generating on 19 May 2020 and reached full capacity on 23 December 2020. In May 2024 Turkey's agriculture ministry (minister İbrahim Yumaklı) said it had produced 9.7 billion kWh in its first four years and added 31 billion lira to the economy, while the regional state water works (DSİ) director, Cihan Aksoy, gave about 9.8 billion kWh and over 31 billion lira for the same period. In July 2020 it was expected to produce about 4.1 billion kWh a year (Daily Sabah; a projection, not a result); the four-year government totals average under 2.5 billion kWh a year. These are government figures; no independent check was found.

shell-dock-sud-villa-inflamable.whole: Shell's Buenos Aires (Dock Sud) refinery processes about 100,000 barrels a day; Shell sold it with about 645 service stations to Brazil's Raízen for US$950 million in 2018 (Oil & Gas Journal), and in May 2026 Raízen was in the final stage of talks to sell its Argentine business, including the refinery (Times Brasil). El Salto reported in September 2025 that the relocation of Villa Inflamable families under the court-ordered clean-up plan had stalled, that ACUMAR's free water deliveries ended in 2024, and, without naming a source, that the Supreme Court closed the Mendoza case in October 2024.

It has been shut since PDVSA's lease expired in 2019; as of November 2025 talks with several would-be operators had failed and the state-owned 2Bays Energy was awaiting a US licence to process Venezuelan crude (Argus).

el-quimbo-emgesa-endesa.whole: Enel started the 400 MW plant in 2015 at a cost of about US$1.2 billion and said it was expected to generate about 2,200 GWh a year, nearly 4% of Colombia's power demand (Enerdata, October 2015; a projection, and no figures on actual output were found). A December 2023 compliance audit by Colombia's Comptroller General found that the six required fishing and tourism ports and the 2,700-hectare irrigation district had still not been built, and that no land had yet been identified for about 1,786 of 3,185 hectares of required forest-compensation land; it rated the environment ministry, ANLA and the regional authority CAM in material non-compliance, with reservations.

occidental-samore-uwa.whole: Occidental stopped drilling the Gibraltar 1 well in 2001 after failing to find oil; earlier estimates, with no source named, had suggested the Samoré block could hold up to 1.5 billion barrels (Amazon Watch, August 2001). In 2004 Colombia's mines minister, Luis Ernesto Mejía, said Oxy had invested about US$60 million without a commercial find and that Ecopetrol, after investing a further US$30 million, had found a Gibraltar gas field able to supply 150 million cubic feet a day for 12 years plus about 15 million barrels of oil equivalent (MercoPress); these are government figures. In July 2016 Portafolio reported the Gibraltar plant supplied gas to about 500,000 families in Norte de Santander, Santander and Antioquia.
